import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/dogs_zurich.csv')

# Set the style of seaborn
sns.set(style="whitegrid")

# Create a count plot to show the distribution of dog breeds
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8))
breed_count = df['Rasse1Text'].value_counts().nlargest(10)
sns.barplot(y=breed_count.index, x=breed_count.values, palette="viridis")

# Add title and labels
plt.title("Top 10 Most Common Dog Breeds in Zurich", fontsize=16)
plt.xlabel("Number of Registered Dogs", fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel("Dog Breed", fontsize=12)

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)

import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/dogs_zurich.csv')

# Set the style of seaborn
sns.set(style="whitegrid")

# Create a count plot to show the distribution of dog breeds
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8))
breed_count = df['Rasse1Text'].value_counts().nlargest(10)
sns.barplot(y=breed_count.index, x=breed_count.values, palette="viridis")

# Add title and labels
plt.title("Top 10 Most Common Dog Breeds in Zurich", fontsize=16)
plt.xlabel("Number of Registered Dogs", fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel("Dog Breed", fontsize=12)

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
